thread.title: Strong iPhone Upgrade Interest Bodes Well For Apple Earnings: Report | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Strong iPhone Upgrade Interest Bodes Well For Apple Earnings: Report | Investor's Business Daily

organizations.name: x bank of america merrill lynch

text:
Survey results point to strong interest among Apple ( AAPL ) iPhone users in upgrading to the company's 12th-generation handsets, a Wall Street investment bank said Tuesday. That bodes well for Apple earnings in fiscal 2019, which started Sept. 30, the firm said.
X Bank of America Merrill Lynch analyst Wamsi Mohan reiterated his buy rating on Apple and predicted the company will report earnings above expectations next year, CNBC reported . He kept his price target of 256 on Apple stock.
Apple rose 1.4% to 226.87 on the stock market today .
Apple stock notched a record high of 233.47 on Oct. 3. It then fell over the next three trading sessions on news reports.

Then, hedge fund Greenlight Capital announced that it had sold off its stake in Apple on concerns about valuation and the impact of Chinese retaliation to U.S. tariffs.
Merrill's Mohan put the focus back on Apple's iPhone business. Apple began selling its high-end XS and XS Max handsets on Sept. 21. It will start selling its midrange XR on Oct. 26 after a week of preorders.
"Our survey suggests interest in upgrading to an iPhone rose significantly in recent months, with steady growth following the announcements of the iPhone XS and iPhone XR," Mohan said in a note to clients.
The firm surveyed nearly 91,000 consumers from March to September. Some 33% of respondents said they plan to upgrade to the iPhone, vs. 15% for Samsung's Galaxy smartphones. Plus, 70% of iPhone owners said they will stick with Apple for their next smartphone purchase.
Apple Earnings Targets Raised Mohan predicts Apple will report fiscal 2019 earnings per share of $14.41 vs. Wall Street's consensus estimate of $13.62.
On Monday, Citi analyst Jim Suva raised his price target on Apple stock to 265 from 230 and kept his buy rating.
Suva raised his Apple earnings estimate for fiscal 2019 to $14.43 from $13.92. He sees Apple benefiting from higher average selling prices for its iPhones during the current product cycle.
"We increase our financial model primarily due to higher ASPs and stronger gross margins given the consumer preference for higher memory configurations of iPhones coupled with the new falling memory prices," he said in a report.
